newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - EAI Select Managers splits duties.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - EAI Select Managers splits duties.

text.p: Some mutual funds hold a widely diversified portfolio of stocks to avoid dependency on a few issues, and make sure that a few poor-performing equities don't cut into the fund's returns.
The EAI Select Managers Equity Fund has taken the notion one step further: It uses five different money management firms to run the fund.
"It gives the portfolio diversification," said Keith Stransky, who manages the managers. "It also gives us market exposure in various areas.
"Some managers have expertise in some areas, and some are institutional-type money managers, who give our clients (certain) exposure."

The five money managers are Dietche & Field Advisers, which manages 30 percent of assets; Iridian Investment Management, 30 percent; Liberty Investment Management, 15 percent; Equinox Capital, 15 percent; and Bennett Lawrence, 10 percent.
According to Stransky, each firm brings its own style. Dietch and Equinox have a value orientation; and Bennett brings an aggressive growth philosophy.
Liberty has a growth orientation, and a focus on cash flow; and Iridian uses the more traditional investing view: Buying stocks is like buying a business.
With all five managers off on their own, one might expect some overlap in buying the same stock. Stransky said it happens about eight percent of the time.
The portfolio holds 225 stocks, with the largest position, International Business Machines Corp, at 1.8 percent.
The top five holdings include IBM; Chase Manhattan Corp; Lockheed Martin Corp, Baxter International Inc; and Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc.
The fund has about four percent of assets in American Depository Receipts and doesn't buy fixed income securities or preferred shares.
"We're a growth fund," said Stransky, "Growth at a reasonable price."

Among its favorite industry sectors, it has 21 percent in consumer cyclicals, such as retailers, restaurants, automakers and media issues; 19 percent in financial services; 18 percent in multi-industry, or conglomerate, stocks; and seven percent in basic industry.
Recent purchases include First Data Corp, which added to an existing stake, and Rite Aid Corp.
Recent sells included Cisco Systems Inc ; Tele-Communications Inc ; Canadian Pacific LTD; Union Texas Petroleum Holdings Inc.
According to Lipper Analytical Services, the fund has returned about 8.50 percent year to date, compared with 13 percent for the average capital appreciation fund.
It placed 149th out of 192 capital appreciations funds, Lipper said.
